successors.name: Neo-Babylonian Empire
successors.text: 'Ammon became a Babylonian province, shortly after being devastated by Nebuchadnezzar II in the 580s BC'

ledger.x: c. 1050 BCE: the Kingdom of Ammon flourishes at Rabbath Ammon. The page's earliest dated entry is 'Kingdom of Ammon flourishes: 11th century BC' and it gives no founding date or founder; King Nahash 'c. 1010 - 990 BC' lay siege to Jabesh-Gilead. A century is not a year; mid-century is a convention.
734 BC: Ammon pays tribute to Assyria.
c. 609 BCE (bridged): Assyria's overlordship ends. No page opened dates when Ammon stopped paying Assyria; the year mirrors the neo-assyrian-empire dossier's close of the 734 tributaries.

c. 609 BCE (bridged): Ammon is under Babylon. 'Ammon flourished during the period of the Neo-Babylonian Empire (626 to 539 BC)'; the Nebuchadnezzar page has the kings of Ammon, Edom, Moab, Sidon and Tyre meeting at Jerusalem in 594 BC to discuss throwing off Babylonian control, and 'In 587 BC, Ammon, Edom and Moab…
580s BC: Babylon turns Ammon into a province.
580s BC: Ammon is annexed by Babylon.
580s BC: the Kingdom of Ammon ends as a province of Babylon.

wars.name: Battle of Qarqar
wars.outcome: Assyrian claim of victory; the coalition's thrones survived.

wars.name: Revolt of Ammon, Edom and Moab against Nebuchadnezzar II
wars.outcome: 'In 587 BC, Ammon, Edom and Moab likewise rebelled'; Ammon was 'devastated by Nebuchadnezzar II in the 580s BC' and became a Babylonian province.

certainty.note: Only the Arnon and Jabbok valleys are named; the Heshbon border with Moab and the northern edge at Gilead are unresolved.
